title: can we add auto approve after x time option to human stages It should default as off.  This can be used for "I want this change to exist in prod for a week or two before I mark it as done" sort of deal or can act as a "speak now or forever hold your peace" pause to get advice but assume no as go.  Crutially this must be done entirely on the backend with a key forcus on scalability as a user may have multiple things under those timers. It is okay if accuracy is sacrificed a bit in support of scalability, as long as the auto approve time is the min it can ever be (as for legal reasons I could see things being required to be held for 10 days etc)

body:
# can we add auto approve after x time option to human stages

It should default as off. 

This can be used for "I want this change to exist in prod for a week or two before I mark it as done" sort of deal or can act as a "speak now or forever hold your peace" pause to get advice but assume no as go. 

Crutially this must be done entirely on the backend with a key forcus on scalability as a user may have multiple things under those timers. It is okay if accuracy is sacrificed a bit in support of scalability, as long as the auto approve time is the min it can ever be (as for legal reasons I could see things being required to be held for 10 days etc)

## Human Correction / Feedback
There is no UI elements this must be configurable in the UI in task stage

# Review Gates

`human` stages and checkpoints park a task in `waiting_human` until you decide. Nothing advances past you silently. For hand-editing files outside a review comment, see `#/docs/develop-alongside`.

## Your three moves

- **Approve / advance** — the task moves to its next stage. Optional guidance is appended to the goal so the next stage inherits your note. When the checkpoint is the last pipeline stage, the button reads "Approve & Mark Complete" because approving finishes the task.
- **Reject with feedback** — feedback is required, and the task fails back to the previous stage with your note attached. You can attach or paste screenshots into the feedback; they ride along so the agent can see the issue (see "Attaching images to a rejection" in Task Images).
- **Re-route** — failback, move, or jump sends the task to a specific stage when neither forward nor back is right.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/tasks/<id>/advance -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"guidance": "Use the existing button styles"}'
curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/tasks/<id>/reject  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"feedback": "Tests still failing on empty input"}'
```

## Review hygiene

- Read the stage **reports** (`GET /tasks/:id/reports`) before deciding — they are the durable record; the activity tail is ephemeral.
- If the inspector has unsaved goal edits, approving first persists them (the editor flushes synchronously), so decide freely.
- A rejected stage re-runs with a freshly curated prompt that includes your feedback — say what was wrong *and* what good looks like.
- `complete` a task only when its pipeline is done; `retry` re-runs a failed stage without a verdict — and restarts its failback/retry budgets from zero, so the next failure auto-retries again.

## Reviewing stage reports line by line

The PR review page has three tabs: **Files Changed** (the git diff),
**Reports**, and **Conversation** (every comment thread). The **Reports** tab
lists each stage markdown report for the task and shows it in its *current
state* — no diff, because with centralised docs the reports live in your
notes store, outside the repository, so they never appear in the git diff.

- Hover any line and click the `⊕` gutter button to leave a line comment;
the report-level `💬` button leaves a whole-report comment. Threads render
inline, exactly like code comments, and use the same sidecar store.
- Toggle **Rendered Preview** to read the formatted markdown; switch back to
**Line Review** to comment.
- **Copy Path**, **Copy Markdown**, and **Notes** open the same report
in your notes workspace.
- Report comments are anchored to the report path and line number and keep the
commented line as an excerpt, so context survives later edits to the report.

The comments you leave on reports (and code) are not just for you:

- On **Pass**, every review comment is written into the `# Human approval`
report and appended to the task goal under `## Human Guidance`, so the next
agent stage receives them as things to consider — you can approve with notes
instead of rejecting.
- On **Fail**, the comments are written into the `# Human rejection` report
and pre-fill the feedback draft (without duplicating text already there).

## Reviewing after merge and deploy

Normally the PR review diff goes empty once the task branch is merged: there
is nothing left unmerged to show. For rapid iteration (merge, deploy, then
review what actually shipped), two per-project settings in Project Settings
(Files & Repos tab) change that:

- **Preserve PR Review Diff After Merge** (default off) — the final review
  keeps showing the merged change, frozen at the merge commit, instead of an
  empty diff.
- **Reset Review Baseline On Each Merge** (default on) — every merge + deploy
  pass starts a fresh baseline. After a fail-back the review shows only the
  code changed in response to the failure; the merged change and the fix-up
  render as two labeled sections, never mixed. Turn it off to keep a
  cumulative view of every pass since the first merge instead.

With both defaults untouched, projects behave exactly as before.

## Automatic approval after a hold

A `human` stage can carry an optional hold (`autoApproveAfterMs`): when a
task has waited at that checkpoint for the full hold, the backend approves
it automatically. Two uses: soak a change ("exist in prod for a week or two
before I mark it as done") and speak-now-or-forever-hold-your-peace pauses
(get advice, assume silence means go). Default is off — stages without a
hold wait forever, exactly as before.

- **Set it per stage** (same every run): open the human stage's Stage
  Settings in the workflow canvas and enable "Auto-approve after hold",
  then pick an amount and unit (minutes / hours / days / weeks; enabling
  defaults to 7 days). The stored form is an integer millisecond count, and
  the save boundary also accepts a human duration string like `10 days`,
  `36 hours`, `1 week`, `90m` (bare numbers mean milliseconds). Saves
  refuse garbage, sub-minute holds (minimum 60s), and holds over 365 days
  with 400.
- **The deadline is a minimum, never exact**: the hold is stamped once when
  the task enters the stage (`autoApproveAt = enteredStageAt + hold`) and
  the timer may fire a little late under load — never early. A 10-day hold
  always lasts at least 10 days.
- **Mid-wait edits don't shorten a live wait**: the stamp is immutable for
  that visit, so changing the hold (or removing it) affects only future
  entries. Tasks already waiting when you configure a hold get no stamp
  until they next enter the stage — move them out and back in to start one.

## 0. Survey status and proposed defaults (needs confirmation)

The grill-me survey (`SURVEY.md`) was generated but **not answered**
(`"answers": {}`). The cited idea file (`idea-20261109-221309.md`) is also
**absent** from the task directory (only `SURVEY.md` is present) — the task
statement text is therefore the authoritative source, and the survey questions
below are answered here as *proposed defaults* (taking every survey
"Recommended" option, which also matches the task text) for the implementer
(or a human) to confirm before building. If confirmed answers arrive later,
they override this section.

| Survey question | Proposed default | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 — Where to set the wait? | **On the step itself (same every run).** | Matches "add option to human stages"; a per-run override is an explicit follow-up, not v1. |
| Q2 — How to pick the length? | **Free-form duration** (`10 days`, `36 hours`, plus a documented bare-number rule). | Covers both use cases in the task ("a week or two", "held for 10 days"); a preset list alone cannot express legal holds. |
| Q3 — What can a person do while waiting? | **Approve or reject early as normal — the timer is only a backup.** | Least surprise; matches the "speak now or forever hold your peace" framing. A "reject-early-only / approve-only-at-deadline" true-hold mode is a follow-up, not v1. |
| Q4 — Warning before auto-approve? | **Yes — one reminder shortly before it approves.** (No snooze/extend in v1.) | A silent auto-approve defeats the "get advice" use case; snooze adds a second mutation surface and can wait. |
| Q5 — How does it show in history? | **Clearly marked as automatic, with timestamps.** | Auditability; the task's own legal-hold framing requires proving *when* and *how* approval happened. |
| Q6 — Timing rule (never early, may be late)? | **Yes — deadline is a minimum; late is fine, early is a bug.** | Stated verbatim in the task ("auto approve time is the min it can ever be"); drives the entire design (§2). |

Implications carried through the rest of the plan:

- v1 is: per-stage optional duration, default off; manual approve/reject
  always win the race; one pre-deadline reminder; auto-approvals are
  unmistakable in history, timeline, and the stage report.
- If Q3 is later answered "true minimum hold" (no early approve), §4.4 and
  the `/advance` route guard must be re-scoped before implementation — that
  answer changes an existing user-facing endpoint, not just new code.
- If Q1 is later answered "both" (per-run override), the per-task deadline
  stamp (§2.2) already supports it: the override would only change what value
  gets stamped at stage entry. No redesign needed.

---

## 1. Goals and non-goals

### 1.1 Goals (acceptance-criteria mapping)

| # | Criterion | Plan section |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | **A human stage can carry an optional auto-approve duration, default off.** Absent/zero means today's behaviour exactly (wait forever). | §4.2 |
| G2 | **A task parked at such a stage auto-advances once its hold has fully elapsed — never before.** The elapsed hold is always `>=` the configured duration, even across restarts, config edits, and clock reads. | §2, §4.3, §4.4 |
| G3 | **Scales to many concurrent timers with O(1) timers.** One sweeper, not one timer per task; bounded work per sweep; no per-task `setTimeout`/`setInterval`. | §2.1, §4.3 |
| G4 | **Manual approve/reject during the wait behave exactly as today and cancel the timer.** No double-advance, no auto-approve after a human already acted. | §4.4, §6.1 |
| G5 | **Auto-approvals are auditable:** history, timeline, stage report, and (where configured) alerts/push all say *automatic*, with the deadline and fire time. | §4.5 |
| G6 | **One pre-deadline reminder** goes out through the existing alert seam shortly before auto-approve (configurable lead time, default sensible, disable-able). | §4.6 |
| G7 | **Change is verifiable:** automated tests pin every behaviour above (incl. never-early and restart recovery); docs updated alongside; `npm run test:unit` + `npm run docs:check` green. | §6, §7 |

### 1.2 Non-goals (explicit follow-ups, not v1)

- True minimum-hold mode (blocking early manual approve) — needs Q3
  confirmation and changes `POST /tasks/:id/advance` semantics.
- Per-run / per-task duration overrides and snooze/extend — needs Q1/Q4
  confirmation; the deadline-stamp design (§2.2) keeps them cheap later.
- Exact-time firing, sub-second precision, or distributed/multi-process
  leader election. v1 assumes the existing single-host scheduler model.
- New UI for configuring the duration. The task mandates backend-only; v1
  exposes the field through the existing stage-config persistence +
  validation so a later UI (or API client) can set it without backend
  changes. A minimal read-back in task payloads (§4.7) is in scope so the
  value is observable.
- New scheduler/queue model, new timer infrastructure (no Redis, no job
  queue, no cron daemon), bulk backfill of deadlines for historical tasks.

---

# Spike notes — auto-approve human stages (E0 / R1+R2)

Date: 2026-11-10. Plan: `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` §0 defaults (all six
"Recommended" options) taken as confirmed; the survey was never answered and
the idea file is absent, so the task text is authoritative.

## R1 — timer/scheduler/persistence truth

1. **Waiting-state durability:** task markdown frontmatter is the persisted
   path (`saveTaskMarkdown` writes keys, `parseTaskMarkdown` reads them in
   `api/work/taskPersistence.js`). `enteredStageAt`/`status` round-trip;
   `resumedAfterInterruption`/`interruptedAt` are the boolean/string
   precedent. `supersededStageId` is memory-only — the new
   `autoApproveAt`/`autoApproveRemindedAt` stamps follow the frontmatter
   path, not the memory-only one.
2. **Sweeper insertion:** second `setInterval` owned by
   `ensureAutoApproveTimer` (own module), armed from `startScheduler`,
   healed from `ensureScheduler`, cleared in `stopScheduler` as
   `store.autoApproveTimer` (unref'd). Honours `schedulerDisabled` and
   `opts.disabled`; sweep cadence 0 disables the sweeper independently.
3. **Auto-advance engine semantics:** the sweeper calls the same
   `store.advanceStage` the `/advance` route calls. `moveToStage` releases
   a `checkpoint`-parked engine on advance-out, so no extra engine handling
   is needed. The sweeper calls `kickScheduler` after any advance so the
   newly entered automated stage dispatches promptly.
4. **Runner-lease interplay:** the sweeper mirrors the `/execute` 409 guard
   (`store.claimStore?.describe(taskId)` → skip when held) and additionally
   skips blocked tasks (`store.isTaskBlocked`), paused stages, and the
   engine's live `running` owner. A `waiting_human` task should never be
   any of these; each guard is one line that closes a double-advance class.
5. **Restart catch-up:** `reconcileInterruptedRuns` only collapses orphaned
   *running* statuses; `waiting_human` tasks are untouched by recovery
   (`parseTaskMarkdown` preserves the status). Stamps persist on disk, so
   the first sweep after boot fires overdue tasks oldest-first within the
   batch cap. No rebuild needed.
6. **Entry sites found (all stamp):** `moveToStage` (covers
   advance/failback/move/jump/reject-failback), `createTask` (created
   directly into a human stage), the `executeStage` human-park block
   (re-park of an `in_stage` task at a human stage via execute/resume/
   retry/follow-up), and the PUT-workflow status flip in
   `api/routes/projects.js`. `parkTaskForSurvey` parks `waiting_human` at
   *agent* stages — excluded by the sweeper's human-stage check, no change.
7. **Exit/clear sites (all clear):** `moveToStage` to any non-qualifying
   destination, `pauseTask`, `abortTask`, `completeTask`,
   `failbackStage`'s abort-policy branch, and the PUT-workflow flip back to
   `in_stage`. One test per exit.

## R2 — duration/config conventions + reminder seam

1. **Duration grammar:** no existing human-duration parser (the config
   `DURATION_PATTERN` returns raw text; `shared/stageDurations.js` parses
   report seconds only). New shared grammar in
   `shared/autoApproveDuration.js`: `ms/s/m/h/d/w` + long/plural forms,
   case-insensitive, multi-part combos (`1h 30m`), whitespace-tolerant.
   **Bare numbers mean milliseconds**, matching the `stage.timeout`
   bare-ms convention. Fractional input rounds UP (`Math.ceil`).
   Min 60s / max 365d enforced ONLY at the stage-save boundary (400);
   `normalizeStage` is shape-only (tolerant read, drops invalid) so
   legacy stages round-trip byte-identically and in-memory/test stages
   can carry short holds without an env escape hatch.
2. **Save boundary:** the four `assertValidStageRunnerPolicies` sites in
   `api/routes/projects.js` gain an `assertValidStageAutoApproves` sibling.
   Non-human stages carrying the field: **kept, not dropped or 400'd**
   (data-preserving across pipeline reorders; only `human` stages act on
   it). Documented in `normalizeStage` JSDoc.
3. **Reminder seam:** two NEW alert events, `task.auto_approve_soon`
   (reminder) and `task.auto_approve` (fired), added to `ALERT_EVENTS`
   (webhook contract tests iterate the list, so coverage is automatic).
   The reminder's UI relay reuses the existing `stage:checkpoint_wait`
   event (no `eventBridge` change); the fired alert needs no UI relay
   (`moveToStage`/`completeTask` already broadcast). Effective lead is
   `min(configured 24h default, half the hold)`; `0` disables reminders.
   Once-per-deadline marker `autoApproveRemindedAt` persisted. No new Web
   Push methods in v1 (follow-up); webhook + dashboard broadcasts cover it.
4. **Frontend tolerance:** stage saves use partial updates
   (`onUpdateStage(id, patch)` merges) and `pipelineTransfer` carries
   unknown keys verbatim — no frontend change needed. Task payloads return
   `{...task}`, so the stamps are visible to API clients with no
   serializer change.

## Test-harness notes (E0.3)

- Stub-store pattern: `taskScheduler.test.js` `makeStore` and
  `stageTransitions.test.js` `makeStore` (mirror both).
- Route pattern: `api/routes/projects.test.js` (temp roots + `app.inject`);
  the app uses the `taskStore` singleton, so integration tests can call
  `taskStore.autoApproveSweep({ now })` with injected time directly.
- Gates per new file: one top-level `function` max
  (`check-one-function-per-file.mjs`; arrow consts exempt) and `@example`
  on every new export (`check-jsdoc-example.mjs`).
- `.env.example` is generated from the config schema — regenerate after
  adding knobs. `freshSchedulerStats` has an exact-shape test to extend.

meta.output:
Settings in the workflow canvas and enable "Auto-approve after hold",
  then pick an amount and unit (minutes / hours / days / weeks; enabling
  defaults to 7 days). The stored form is an integer millisecond count, and
  the save boundary also accepts a human duration string like `10 days`,
  `36 hours`, `1 week`, `90m` (bare numbers mean milliseconds). Saves
  refuse garbage, sub-minute holds (minimum 60s), and holds over 365 days
  with 400.
- **The deadline is a minimum, never exact**: the hold is stamped once when
  the task enters the stage (`autoApproveAt = enteredStageAt + hold`) and
  the timer may fire a little late under load — never early. A 10-day hold
  always lasts at least 10 days.
- **Mid-wait edits don't shorten a live wait**: the stamp is immutable for
  that visit, so changing the hold (or removing it) affects only future
  entries. Tasks already waiting when you configure a hold get no stamp
  until they next enter the stage — move them out and back in to start one.
- **Humans always win the race**: approve or reject early as normal and the
  timer is cancelled — no double-advance, no auto-approve after you acted.
  Pausing, aborting, moving, or completing also cancels the wait; coming
  back starts a fresh full hold. Simply re-running a task that never left
  the checkpoint keeps its original deadline.
- **One reminder**: shortly before the deadline (24h out, or half the hold
  for short holds) a `task.auto_approve_soon` webhook fires once per wait,
  naming the deadline. Set `KAINBAIN_AUTO_APPROVE_REMINDER_LEAD_MS=0` to
  turn reminders off.
- **Audit trail**: the history line, timeline row (badged `automated`), the
  `# Human approval (automatic)` report, and the `task.auto_approve`
  webhook all name the hold, the deadline, and the fire time.

Operators: the sweeper runs on its own slow cadence
(`KAINBAIN_AUTO_APPROVE_SWEEP_MS`, default 60s; `0` disables it while
stamps persist) and advances at most `KAINBAIN_AUTO_APPROVE_BATCH`
(default 25) tasks per pass, oldest deadline first. Health is visible in
`GET /engine/state` (`autoApproved`, `autoApproveDeferred`, …). Restarts
are safe: deadlines live on disk, so the first sweep after boot fires
overdue waits oldest-first.
